text:
The Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) announced Thursday its incumbent commissioner, Heo Koo-youn, has been unanimously elected for a third term beginning in January 2027.
The KBO's board of governors, made up of the 10 club owners, submitted their written votes Wednesday to elect him as its 26th commissioner, more than three weeks after the board of directors, comprising club presidents, had unanimously nominated Heo as commissioner.
Heo, 75, became the third commissioner in KBO history to win three consecutive terms, following former commissioners Park Yong-oh and Koo Bon-neung. Heo's new three-year term is set to begin in January 2027.
Heo, a longtime television color commentator, was first elected commissioner in March 2022 to succeed Chung Ji-taik, who stepped down abruptly because of health issues. Heo served the remainder of Chung's term, which ended on Dec. 31, 2023. Heo was unanimously reelected as the KBO's 25th commissioner in November that year.
